repo_overview.summary: Multi-agent framework on smolagents that automates the research lifecycle from idea to LaTeX paper. A ManagerAgent (CodeAgent) orchestrates six specialized sub-agents (ideation, experimentation, resource preparation, writeup, reviewer, proofreading), each with its own LLM loop, which coordinate through a shared per-run workspace directory under results/. Experiments are delegated to a vendored AI-Scientist-v2 tree-search pipeline run as a subprocess.

components.purpose: entry point: redirects logs to files, registers Phoenix tracing, resolves model config (CLI > .llm_config.yaml > defaults), creates or resumes (--resume) a workspace, builds the agent system and runs manager.run(task)

BaseResearchAgent (CodeAgent subclass), the ManagerAgent and six sub-agents (typocheck_agent.py exists but is not wired in utils.py); context_compaction.py holds context monitoring and compaction as a step callback
create_model, initialize_agent_system (sub-agents become managed_agents of the manager, each receives the interrupt step callback), save_agent_memory
LLM client helpers, .llm_config.yaml loading with a parameter filter wrapped around litellm.completion, CLI arguments
per-agent system prompts and instructions, research planning templates, workspace conventions

agent tools: idea generation, novelty check, paper search, run_experiment_tool.py (subprocess wrapper around external_tools); writeup/ holds LaTeX, plotting and VLM review tools; general_tools/ holds web search, text browser, file editing, arXiv, KB/repo indexing, talk_to_user
WorkspacePythonExecutor: executes agent-generated code inside the workspace directory with an import whitelist
socket-based interrupt channel and a step callback that injects user input into a running agent (human-in-the-loop)

vendored AI-Scientist-v2 (best-first tree search over experiment code, plotting, writeup, LLM/VLM review); third-party code, coded only up to the subprocess boundary in run_experiment_tool.py

topology.justification: The ManagerAgent is a CodeAgent that receives six sub-agents as managed_agents: ideation, experimentation, resource_preparation, writeup, reviewer and proofreading (utils.py:315-323, manager_agent.py:168-175). Each sub-agent is itself a BaseResearchAgent/CodeAgent with its own name, description, system prompt, tools, step callbacks and step/max_steps loop (utils.py:240-248). smolagents exposes them to the manager as callable units, and a delegated helper with its own LLM loop counts as an agent. resilience.name: automatic token-threshold context compaction
resilience.what_it_is: A ContextMonitoringCallback is appended to the step_callbacks of every BaseResearchAgent. After each ActionStep it estimates the context size (characters / 4, plus 500 characters per tool, plus 3500 tokens constant overhead) and compares it against 75% of the model context limit. When the estimate exceeds the threshold, agent.memory.steps is replaced by one synthetic ActionStep holding a rule-based summary (tool call counts, top 5 observations truncated to 200 chars, last 2 reasoning outputs, last 3 errors, last 3 outputs) plus up to 3 recent steps with content. The summary is built without an LLM call.
resilience.function_in_system: Runs as a step callback after every action step of the manager and all six sub-agents, so it bounds the prompt each agent sends on its next model call. Guards long research runs against context window overflow and ever-growing per-call cost. Otherwise a long agent run hits the provider context limit and the call fails, or the cost per step keeps rising with the history.

resilience.name: workspace and agent-memory resume of a previous run
resilience.what_it_is: launch_multiagent.py --resume <dir> reuses an existing workspace directory; without --task the manager receives a continuation task telling it to analyze the existing files and progress the research. Memory files are written by save_agent_memory only after manager.run() returns successfully.
resilience.function_in_system: Sits at system start, before the manager loop begins. Lets an interrupted or finished multi-hour research run continue with the ideas, experiment results and drafts already in the workspace. After a crash the memory files are missing, so continuation then relies on the workspace files plus the continuation task. Otherwise every interruption forces a full restart, repeating all LLM and experiment cost.

resilience.name: quota-aware retry with exponential backoff on agent model calls
resilience.what_it_is: LoggingLiteLLMModel.generate wraps every agent LLM call in a retry loop: up to 5 retries with delay 9s * 2^attempt (9, 18, 36, 72, 144 s), triggered only when the exception text contains '429', 'RateLimitError', 'RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED' or 'quota'. Any other exception, or the final failed attempt, is re-raised immediately.
resilience.function_in_system: Sits around model.generate() of the manager and all sub-agents, since BaseResearchAgent wraps every model with this logger when a workspace is set. Tools receive the raw unwrapped model (get_raw_model, 'Tools get raw model for efficiency'), so the retry covers the agents' own decision calls only. Absorbs provider rate-limit and quota errors that long multi-agent research runs predictably hit. Otherwise a single 429 aborts the agent step and can propagate up to crash the whole run.

resilience.name: socket-based human interrupt and instruction injection
resilience.what_it_is: At startup a TCP server is always started (default 127.0.0.1:5001, usable via nc) that pushes received lines into a queue. Every agent (manager and all six sub-agents) gets a step callback that polls the queue without blocking after each step. On 'interrupt', 'stop' or 'pause' the agent pauses, reads a multi-line instruction, asks whether it is a modification (m) or a new task (n), and appends it to the agent memory as a UserInstructionStep ('Additional instruction from the user: ...') or as a new TaskStep before resuming.
resilience.function_in_system: Hooks into the step boundary of every agent loop, so a human can halt any agent mid-run and redirect it while keeping all accumulated state. The README advertises it as real-time human-in-the-loop intervention. Otherwise a run heading in the wrong direction can only be killed and restarted from scratch.

resilience.name: workspace-bound code execution with import allowlist
resilience.what_it_is: Agent-generated Python code runs in WorkspacePythonExecutor, a LocalPythonExecutor subclass that os.chdir()s into the workspace directory before each execution and restores the original directory in a finally block. Imports are restricted to the essential_imports allowlist (stdlib, config libs, HF datasets/transformers, wandb, tqdm, archives), which smolagents' LocalPythonExecutor enforces. The chdir provides path scoping only and leaves absolute paths reachable.
resilience.function_in_system: Wraps every code action of the manager and sub-agents. Keeps all agents writing into the shared per-run workspace they coordinate through, and the allowlist blocks unapproved modules so heavy ML work is routed through RunExperimentTool ('tool-centric agents (no direct ML library access)'). Otherwise agents scatter files relative to the launch directory and can run arbitrary libraries directly in the orchestrator process.

resilience.name: success-criteria gate before writeup agent termination
resilience.what_it_is: The WriteupAgent registers validate_success_criteria as a smolagents final_answer_check. Before any final answer is accepted it checks in order: final_paper.tex exists, final_paper.pdf exists, a VLM validation of the PDF reports no error and publication_ready, and LaTeXContentVerificationTool reports all_criteria_met (required sections, >15000 content chars, at least 3 figures, citations, references.bib). Any failure raises ValueError('TERMINATION_BLOCKED: ...') carrying a concrete list of issues. The agent step budget is raised to max_steps=150 to leave room for the resulting rework. The VLM step is defective: for a PDF with analysis_focus 'pdf_validation' the tool routes to _analyze_pdf_comprehensively, whose result carries no overall_assessment key, so publication_ready always evaluates to False and the gate raises TERMINATION_BLOCKED on every attempt. The writeup agent therefore ends only through its max_steps limit.
resilience.function_in_system: Sits at the termination point of the writeup agent loop, between the agent proposing final_answer and the answer being returned to the manager. Catches premature or false success claims: missing, corrupted or incomplete papers. The raised error is fed back so the agent keeps working on the listed issues. Otherwise the writeup agent can report completion to the manager without a valid, complete PDF.

resilience.name: reviewer-score quality gate with issue-type routing

The manager system prompt forbids termination below a reviewer score of 6 and prescribes a decision matrix: presentation issues go back to WriteupAgent, experimental issues to ExperimentationAgent, conceptual issues to IdeationAgent, followed by a re-review. It also obliges the manager to analyze every sub-agent output against listed success and failure indicators before proceeding.
resilience.function_in_system: Implements a cross-agent critic loop at the orchestration level: an independent agent evaluates the final artifact and the manager routes the failure to the pipeline stage that caused it. Otherwise the manager declares the task complete regardless of review outcome.

resilience.name: prompt-level iteration caps with stagnation-based escalation
resilience.what_it_is: The manager prompt caps delegation at 3 calls per agent and 12 agent calls per project, tracked only as a 'mental count' by the model. It defines escalation when caps are hit (writeup failing 3 times with the same issues goes back to experimentation, experimentation failing 3 times goes back to ideation, all agents at the limit means terminating with the best result and an explanation of remaining issues) and stagnation indicators (scores flat after 2 iterations, recurring issues, agents unable to resolve core problems).
resilience.function_in_system: Bounds the reviewer-driven revision loop at the orchestration level. Guards against endless writer/reviewer ping-pong and the cost and runtime it causes. The limit relies entirely on the model counting correctly. Otherwise the quality gate can keep the run cycling indefinitely.

evidence.snippet:
**MAXIMUM ITERATION LIMITS** (Prevent endless cycles):
- **Per Agent**: Maximum 3 iterations per agent per workflow
- **Total Workflow**: Maximum 12 total agent calls per research project
- **Quality vs. Efficiency**: Balance quality improvement with practical constraints

**ESCALATION STRATEGY** (When hitting limits):
1. **If WriteupAgent hits 3 iterations with same issues**: Consider if experiments are fundamentally flawed → ExperimentationAgent
2. **If ExperimentationAgent hits 3 iterations**: Consider if idea is infeasible → IdeationAgent  
3. **If all agents hit limits**: Terminate with best available result and detailed explanation of remaining issues

**STAGNATION INDICATORS** (Consider termination if seeing):
- ❌ ReviewerAgent scores not improving after 2 iterations
- ❌ Same issues recurring despite agent claims of fixes
- ❌ Agents reporting inability to resolve core problems

resilience.name: prompt rules against code-action execution failures
resilience.what_it_is: The shared system prompt template adds rule 9 for all agents: always close triple-quoted strings and prefer string concatenation for multiline content. The ExperimentationAgent prompt repeats these syntax requirements. The ResourcePreparationAgent prompt demands incremental processing in small single-purpose code blocks across multiple steps, since a failure anywhere in a large block forces regenerating the whole block.

Otherwise agents lose steps and budget to syntax errors and repeated regeneration of large failing blocks.

evidence.snippet: 9. STRING SYNTAX: Always properly close triple-quoted strings with three double quotes. For multiline content, prefer string concatenation (e.g., "Line 1" + " Line 2") over triple-quoted strings to avoid syntax errors.

CODE SYNTAX REQUIREMENTS:
- ALWAYS properly terminate triple-quoted strings with three double quotes
- When using f-strings with triple quotes, ensure complete closure
- For multiline strings, use simple string concatenation instead of triple quotes
- Example: outcome = "Line 1" + " Line 2" + " Line 3" (GOOD)
- Example: outcome = f"Line 1 Line 2" (PROPER SYNTAX)
- NEVER leave triple-quoted strings unclosed

## Avoid Monolithic Code Blocks

**Break large operations into focused, single-purpose steps.** Attempting to process entire directory trees, generate all file descriptions, and build complete text files in one massive code block leads to syntax errors and execution failures. Instead, use incremental processing: create the directory structure first, then systematically process files in small batches across multiple tool calls. When any part of a large block fails, the entire operation must be regenerated, wasting tokens and increasing failure probability.

resilience.name: LLM idea standardization with rule-based fallback
resilience.what_it_is: IdeaStandardizationTool strips line-number prefixes left by see_file output, parses the idea (taking the first element of a list), and asks the raw model to map it to the AI-Scientist-v2 schema. The response is parsed from a json code block, a bare JSON object or the whole text, and validated for the six fields Name, Title, Short Hypothesis, Abstract, Experiments, Risk Factors and Limitations (present and non-empty). On any failure a rule-based conversion maps common field names, derives a Name from the title and synthesizes default experiments and risk factors. If parsing the input itself fails, the tool returns a placeholder idea named conversion_failed that carries all fields the RunExperimentTool schema check requires.
resilience.function_in_system: Sits in the ExperimentationAgent path directly before the idea schema validation of RunExperimentTool, which the prompt makes mandatory. Converts heterogeneous idea formats produced by the manager and ideation agent into the input format of the vendored pipeline and keeps the conversion working when the LLM output is unparsable or incomplete. Otherwise a malformed or differently structured idea stops the experiment step or reaches the pipeline without model and dataset specifications.

resilience.name: workspace-grounded generation prompt in LaTeXGeneratorTool
resilience.what_it_is: Before each section generation the tool scans paper_workspace/figures for .png files with their .txt descriptions and reads the citation keys and titles from references.bib, and inserts both lists into the system prompt. The prompt requires the exact figure filenames in \includegraphics, citation keys from the list, a [CITE:brief_description] placeholder when no key fits, and numerical values only from the content_description passed by the agent, stating that the model has no access to experimental data files.
resilience.function_in_system: Sits inside the tool-internal LLM call that writes the paper sections for the WriteupAgent. Restricts generated LaTeX to figures, references and results that exist in the workspace, and hands unmatched citations to the automatic placeholder resolution of LaTeXCompilerTool. Otherwise the model invents figure files, citation keys and results that break compilation or end up as fabricated claims in the paper.
